rationale.correct: Latent load of 12 kW represents energy required to remove water vapor from indoor air. Water phase-change enthalpy (latent heat of vaporization) ≈ 2.45 MJ/kg at room temperature. Condensation rate = 12 kW ÷ 2.45 MJ/kg = 12,000 J/s ÷ 2.45 × 10⁶ J/kg ≈ 4.9 kg/hr of water removed. Density of water ≈ 1 kg/L, so condensation ≈ 4.9 L/hr minimum. In practice, specify 6–8 L/hr drain capacity to account for coil inefficiencies, surge during startup, and safety margin. Drain line must slope ≥1:80 (1/8 unit vertical in 10 units horizontal) per PD 1058 Rule VIII Section 811(e). Source: LEA-UTIL-002-04 Tropical Climate Considerations; ASHRAE humid climate design.
rationale.takeaway: Latent load conversion to condensate rate requires dividing thermal energy (kW) by water latent heat (~2.45 MJ/kg); specify drain capacity 50% higher than calculated minimum for tropical climate redundancy and coil surge protection.
